header: How the engine decides which executive briefing is the best one. A model never answers the same question the same way twice, so I ask the engine for several candidates and score every one with THIS function (plain code: no model, no randomness, the same briefing always gets the same score). It keeps the highest and stores it (edsStore.ts). Whatever is stored is what every later ask of that question shows, until the archive of circulars changes. The score is out of 100: 30 grounding every figure is in the circulars (12), every number 3..31 is written in them too, as digits or as words (6), the words of the findings and the table are words of the circulars (12) 25 coverage the briefing speaks of what the question asks (its key words are in the briefing) 25 structure an overview (5), 3-6 findings (8), and for a "compare ..." question a complete table with a column per side (12) 10 charts each chart has a title, a sentence saying what it shows, a unit, 2+ labelled items, both series named, one unit on one axis 10 citations every finding names the circular it comes from The score ranks candidates and keeps out a poor one; it does not prove a briefing true. The proof that a figure exists is the grounding step in executiveSynthesis.ts (a figure that is in no circular is removed before the score is taken).

members.name: parts
members.type: { grounding: number; coverage: number; structure: number; charts: number; citations: number }

members.name: sourceText
doc: The text of the circulars the briefing was written from.

members.name: droppedFigures
doc: How many figures the grounding step had to remove from this candidate; each one is a figure the model made up.

members.name: labels
doc: The archive's own names for the circulars ("Circular 007 (2026)"); I do not treat their numbers as claims.

members.name: qualifiersBySource
doc: Per circular id: the qualifiers its SUBJECT LINE puts in brackets ("Mid-term inclusion"), which are the circular's own name for the situation.

members.name: verification
doc: The second reading (edsVerify.ts): sentences it had to remove as unsupported, and reports the code could not check and left alone.

members.name: amendments
doc: Circulars that correct, amend or extend ANOTHER circular among the sources: `id` amends the circulars in `amends`.

symbols.name: subjectQualifiers
doc: Returns the bracketed qualifiers of a circular's subject line. "Sub: Revised GPAIS amount (Mid-term inclusion) for contract workers" tells WHAT the amounts are: a briefing that calls them "monthly deposits" that "decrease" has lost the circular's own meaning, so I rate a briefing that carries the qualifier as better.

doc: Returns true when a unit says "parts of one whole" cannot apply: multiples, ratios, rates, durations. The chart-type rule shares this function.

symbols.name: pickBest
symbols.sig: export function pickBest<T extends { result: SynthesisResult; score: BriefingScore }>(cands: T[]): T | null
symbols.generics: T extends { result: SynthesisResult; score: BriefingScore }
doc: Picks the best of several scored candidates. The higher total wins; a tie goes to the better coverage, then to the one whose canonical JSON sorts first, so I get the same winner from the same candidates whatever order they arrived in.
